sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 5.4% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F177].
Revenue fell 32.5% in FY2020 to $94.5 billion, then rose 64.7% in FY2021 and 51.5% in FY2022 to $236 billion [F5][D153][F6][D192][F7][D232].
The FY2022 jump came from higher upstream realizations and downstream margins [P57].
Since then revenue has fallen three straight years, down 16.5% in FY2023 and 4.6% in FY2025 to $184 billion [F8][D274][F10][D358].
The FY2025 decline reflected lower crude oil and refined product prices, partly offset by higher volumes [P17].
Chevron U.S.A. Inc. supplied 75.1% of FY2025 revenue and subtracted 3.9pp from growth [D402][D404].
Tengizchevroil was the offset, growing 16.5% and adding 1.5pp on an 11.6% revenue share [D419][D420][D418].
U.S. upstream revenue rose 34.0% on the Hess acquisition and Permian and Gulf of America growth [D553][P24].
Net income fell 30.5% against a 4.6% revenue decline, so operating costs did not flex with the top line [F20][D359][F10][D358].
Diluted EPS fell 31.8%, slightly worse than net income as the diluted share count rose 2.1% [F50][D361][D374].
Net margin was 6.7% in FY2025, below the 7.9% window median and far under the 15.1% FY2022 high [F30][D613][D612].
Cost of revenue fell to 57.2% of revenue from 58.8%, while SG&A rose to 2.7% from 2.4% [D338][D296][D340][D298].
SG&A rose 6.0% on the Hess acquisition and higher professional service costs [D372][P13].
Depreciation, depletion and amortization rose to 10.7% of revenue on higher production and higher rates [D341][P12].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.8% from 35.5%, widening the gap between operating and net margin [D345][D303].
Operating cash flow rose 7.8% to $33.9 billion, 2.76x net income and above the 1.97x window median [F60][D362][D346][D644].
Higher cash distributions from TCO and legacy Hess assets more than offset lower commodity prices [P6].
Free cash flow was $16.6 billion, an 8.8% margin against a 8.9% window median [F80][D343][D616].
Capex of $17.3 billion was 9.2% of revenue and 0.86x D&A [F70][D342][D348].
Cash and investments were $7.3 billion at FY2025, down 11.8% [D349][D375].
Total assets jumped 26.1% to $324 billion and equity 22.4% to $186 billion, consistent with the Hess acquisition [F110][D365][F176][D367].
Return on average equity was 7.3%, in the 17th percentile of six energy peers against a 14.9% median [D357][D641][D642].
Buybacks and dividends of $24.8 billion were 149.7% of free cash flow, funded partly by $11.4 billion of debt issued [D353][D354][X157].
Revenue has fallen three years running, from $197 billion in FY2023 to $184 billion in FY2025 [F8][F10][R1].
Payouts exceeded free cash flow in each of those years, at 132.8%, 179.7% and 149.7% [D270][D312][D354][R4].
The table's revenue is a later recast for FY2018 through FY2025, so growth mixing recast and first-reported years is not like-for-like [R3][F10][X10].
Long-term debt is not reported after FY2021, so net cash and debt growth cannot be tracked across the break [R12][X193].
If FY2026 revenue falls below the FY2025 level of $184 billion, the three-year decline extends [F10].
Free cash flow margin below its 8.9% window median would keep payouts above free cash flow [D616][D354].
Organic capex guided at $18-19 billion for 2026 exceeds FY2025's $17.3 billion, which would pressure free cash flow [P4][F70].
